content:
Maya Chen: hey all, first-week onboarding question. I can auth to Okta and the VPN says connected, but i can't reach git.internal.redwood.com. browser times out, and `git clone` fails with DNS resolved to 10.10.0.23 but that IP is my home router.

Lucas Park: welcome Maya! that sounds like a classic CIDR overlap. what does `ip route` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` show on your machine? also are you on personal wifi or office network?

Maya Chen: on personal wifi (xfinity). here's the output: 
``n$ ip route
default via 192.168.1.1 dev wlp2s0 proto dhcp metric 600
10.10.0.0/24 via 192.168.1.1 dev wlp2s0 proto dhcp metric 600
172.23.0.0/16 via 172.23.5.1 dev wg0 proto static metric 50
```
`/etc/resolv.conf` shows corporate DNS 172.23.5.2 but lookup for git.internal.redwood.com returns 10.10.0.23 (local router) when i ping it.

IT Support: ah yep, your home LAN is using 10.10.0.0/24 which overlaps with our git host (10.10.0.0/16). VPN pushes the corporate route but the kernel prefers the more specific /24 on your local NIC so traffic never goes over wg0.

Maya Chen: is there a way to force traffic over the VPN without changing my home router? i'm renting, can't reconfigure it easily.

network-ops: two safe options: 1) use a phone hotspot (creates a different subnet) or 2) add a host route that sends the git IP via the VPN gateway. e.g. on linux: `sudo ip route replace 10.10.0.23/32 via 172.23.5.1 dev wg0` — that will ensure traffic for that host goes to the tunnel.

Maya Chen: ok i'll try the host route. will that persist across reconnects?

Lucas Park: no, it won't persist by default. if you reconnect the VPN the route table may be reprogrammed. For a temporary fix it's fine. For a more stable solution we usually recommend using the phone hotspot or asking IT to NAT the source for new-hires, or change the bastion/host IP if feasible.

Maya Chen: tried the command and now `curl -I https://git.internal.redwood.com` returns `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` — nice! thanks.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-4922: "New-hire CIDR overlap guidance and onboarding note". Assigned to network-ops.

okta-bot: User Maya Chen (maya.chen@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2025-12-05T08:45:02Z

network-ops: we'll add a line to the onboarding doc: "If your home LAN overlaps with corporate IPs, prefer hotspot or run a host route while onboarding. Contact IT for a one-time NAT workaround." Also adding a FAQ entry for common home subnets (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, etc.).

SRE Oncall: small follow-up: if you run multiple services that collide, host routes become tedious. If you see repeated issues we can provision a dev VPN profile that SNATs your traffic to a non-overlapping egress IP. Ping #it-support to request it.

Maya Chen: awesome, that solves it for now. i'll add a note in my onboarding checklist and switch to hotspot if i need to keep working. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
